Nina (PM): Quick proposal — defining formal benchmark gates + customer commit flow for model lifecycle transitions. I sketched a minimal gate set and a suggestion for how customers opt into migration windows. Want quick reactions before I turn into a doc.
Sylas (Eng): LGTM overall. Need to split gates by model family and by expected seq-length buckets tho. p95 is useless if we mix 2k and 16k contexts.
Maria (Research): Agreed with Sylas. Also recommend a mixed automated + human eval requirement. Automated checks for perf/regression, then a small human eval sample for safety/quality checks.
Jonah (Customer Success): From customer side — migration windows need to be longer for enterprises. Also we should offer a paid assisted migration option and a clear opt-out that preserves pinning for contracts.
Lena (Prod Ops): Can we be explicit about ship dates and comms? proposal should include: (1) initial kickoff email, (2) 30/14/7 day reminders, (3) console banners + per-customer flags. Also alerting for rollback readiness.
Nina (PM): Draft gate thresholds (proposal):
```
- Latency: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 230ms (per seq-length bucket)
- Cost: <= 2x current per-token spend or provide quantized variant that meets cost delta 
- Quality: automated eval pass >= 92% on canary prompt set; human eval: no statistically significant drop vs baseline on 300 checks
- Safety: hallucination/TOX metrics under threshold (TBD)
- Stability: <0.1% error rate across 48h canary
```
Open to numbers — want concrete so eng can run preflight checks.
Sylas (Eng): p95 230ms might be tight for larger models at 16k. Suggest these buckets: <=2k, <=8k, >8k and p95 targets: 180/320/600 respectively. Also require KV cache warm-up run before canary measurement.
Maria (Research): For automated eval we should include a quality holdout that mirrors customer usage: instruction-following, multi-step reasoning, and safety prompts. Recommend at least 1k synthetic + 300 human checks as Nina suggested.
Jonah (Customer Success): On the opt-in mechanics — propose: staged cohorts A/B/C. Cohort A = 5 strategic customers (manual outreach). Cohort B = self-serve opt-in with 60d window. Cohort C = default switch with 120d notice for standard customers. Billing note: prorated pricing on cutover day unless customer signs migration support.
Lena (Prod Ops): Implementation notes: console flag per-customer, ribbon banner, change-log entry, and a dashboard card with these metrics: latency by bucket, canary pass/fail, customer opt-in state. We can reuse rollout APIs. Need owners for engineering dashboarding and email templates.
Nina (PM): Decision proposal:
- Finalize thresholds by EOD Fri (owners: Sylas for perf, Maria for eval thresholds)
- Pilot cohort A next sprint (owners: Jonah + Eng SE)
- Communication cadence: 60d public window by default, 120d for enterprise holdouts
- Offer paid migration support + pin-exemption clause in contracts
Anyone object?
Sylas (Eng): No objection. Will run perf matrix across families and post numbers by Thu.
Maria (Research): No objection. I’ll attach the eval harness and draft human eval plan by Thu.
Jonah (Customer Success): Fine but request 90d default instead of 60d for standard. Many customers need procurement lead time.
Lena (Prod Ops): 90d SGTM. I’ll sketch comm templates and the dashboard card. Owner for rollout automation: @Sylas.
Nina (PM): Ok updated: default window 90d. Action items:
- Sylas: perf matrix + KV warm-up plan (due Thu)
- Maria: eval harness + 300 human checks plan (due Thu)
- Jonah: recruit cohort A customers and prepare outreach copy (due Mon)
- Lena: comm templates + dashboard card stub (due Fri)
- Nina: finalize gate doc and PR to product repo (due Fri)
deploy-bot: Canary cluster created for cohort-A testing (id: canary-2024-1765439999) :white_check_mark:
Jonah (Customer Success): thanks — I’ll ping legal about pin-exemption wording after I confirm cohort list.
Nina (PM): Good progress. Quick last Q — do we want an explicit rollback SLA if canary fails? propose auto-fallback to pinned model for affected requests and a 24h incident review window.
Sylas (Eng): Yes auto-fallback + 24h block is good. We'll implement graceful fallback in routing layer and add a metric to the dashboard.
Maria (Research): Also log human-eval failures to the eval-tracker so we can trace regressions to prompt clusters.
Lena (Prod Ops): I'll add rollback steps to the runbook and a short incident template for the 24h review.
Nina (PM): Great — locking this plan. I’ll open the formal RFC and tag owners. Next sync: Thu 10am for perf + eval results. Thanks everyone :rocket:
